reason: E2 shows that SRO structures in bulk CoFeNiCr have better thermal stability (lower Gibbs free energy change with temperature) than random structures, supporting the core premise that SRO enhances stability. However, E1 indicates that experimental detection of SRO in multi-principal element HEAs is currently lacking, which undermines the premise that SRO can be reliably measured in the proposed experiment. The cited evidence does not address nanoparticle melting or the effect of SRO on premelting/melting temperatures, leaving key premises about nanoparticle behavior unsupported.
premises: Chemical SRO enhances thermal stability of bulk HEAs
SRO can be induced by annealing in HEAs
SRO is experimentally detectable in multi-principal element alloys
Melting behavior of nanoparticles is sensitive to atomic-scale ordering
